title: Ninth Word Fourth Point Reminders Of Afternoon Sunset And Night

questions.question: What season, stage of life, and period in history are linked with the time of 'Asr?
questions.answer: It is connected with autumn, old age, and the time of the Final Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: What does the 'Asr time help a person remember besides those three comparisons?
questions.answer: It reminds a person of Allah’s actions and merciful gifts shown in those times.

questions.question: What three major endings does Maghrib bring to mind?
questions.answer: It brings to mind the end of many living things, the death of a human being, and the destruction of the world at the start of resurrection.

questions.question: According to the passage, what effect should Maghrib have on a careless person?
questions.answer: It should wake the person up from being unaware and spiritually asleep.

questions.question: What does 'Isha make a person think about in the visible world?
questions.answer: It makes a person think of darkness covering the world and winter covering the dead earth.

questions.question: What does the passage say happens even to the traces people leave behind after they die?
questions.answer: Their remaining works also fade away and pass into forgetfulness.

questions.question: What does 'Isha remind a person about this worldly life as a whole?
questions.answer: It reminds the person that this world of testing will one day be closed completely.

questions.question: Which prayer time especially points to Allah’s majesty and overpowering rule through images of darkness, ending, and closure?
questions.answer: 'Isha does.

questions.question: How is the afternoon prayer time compared to human life?
questions.answer: It is compared to old age.

questions.question: How is the afternoon prayer time compared to the natural world?
questions.answer: It is compared to autumn.

questions.question: How is the afternoon prayer time compared to sacred history?
questions.answer: It is compared to the blessed age of the Final Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: Why is Maghrib a strong reminder for the human heart?
questions.answer: Because it points to loss, death, and the end of the world, which shake a person out of heedlessness.

questions.question: What two divine qualities are especially remembered at Maghrib?
questions.answer: Allah’s glory and greatness.

questions.question: During 'Isha, what examples are given of things becoming hidden or covered?
questions.answer: Daytime things are covered by darkness, and the earth in winter is covered like something prepared for burial.

questions.question: What idea about human achievements is taught through the description of 'Isha?
questions.answer: Human works do not last forever; they too disappear from memory.

questions.question: What common theme connects 'Asr, Maghrib, and 'Isha in this passage?
questions.answer: All three remind a person of decline, ending, and returning to Allah’s power and mercy.

questions.question: What does the passage connect with 'Asr in terms of the year, a person’s life, and the Muslim community’s history?
questions.answer: It connects 'Asr with autumn, old age, and the time of the Final Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: What is remembered through those comparisons at 'Asr?
questions.answer: Allah’s deeds and His favors are remembered.

questions.question: What part of the year is mentioned with Maghrib?
questions.answer: The end of autumn.

questions.question: What personal event is mentioned with Maghrib?
questions.answer: A person’s death.

questions.question: What world-changing event is also mentioned with Maghrib?
questions.answer: The destruction of the world at the beginning of resurrection.

questions.question: What spiritual problem is Maghrib meant to fight against?
questions.answer: Carelessness and forgetfulness about deeper realities.

questions.question: What does nightfall do to the things seen in daytime?
questions.answer: It hides them under darkness.

questions.question: What larger truth does 'Isha teach by mentioning darkness, winter, forgotten works, and the closing of the world?
questions.answer: It teaches that everything in this life passes away and that Allah’s powerful control rules over all endings.

questions.question: Which prayer time is described with examples of decline rather than beginnings?
questions.answer: 'Asr is described that way.

questions.question: In what way does 'Asr match autumn and old age?
questions.answer: All of them point to the later stage of something that is moving toward its end.

questions.question: Why might the Era of Bliss be mentioned with 'Asr?
questions.answer: To connect that prayer time with an important stage in sacred history and with remembering Allah’s mercy in it.

questions.question: What does Maghrib teach a person by reminding him of death and the end of the world?
questions.answer: It teaches that worldly life is temporary and that a person should not stay careless.

questions.question: What feeling should these reminders at Maghrib create toward Allah?
questions.answer: They should create awe before His greatness and majesty.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the coming of night at 'Isha?
questions.answer: It describes night as covering the world and hiding what was seen in the day.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the fading of the works of dead people?
questions.answer: To show that even what people leave behind does not remain forever.

questions.question: What view of this world is taught through the description of 'Isha?
questions.answer: This world is a temporary testing place that will one day come to a complete close.

questions.question: What three comparisons are used to explain the meaning of 'Asr?
questions.answer: The passage compares it to autumn, to old age, and to the time of the Final Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: What do those comparisons help believers notice about Allah?
questions.answer: They help believers notice His actions and His merciful blessings.

questions.question: How does Maghrib move from nature to human life to the end of the world?
questions.answer: It begins with creatures passing away, then points to human death, and then points to the world’s destruction before resurrection.

questions.question: What does this progression at Maghrib suggest about endings?
questions.answer: It suggests that endings happen at many levels, from individual lives to the whole world.

questions.question: What images are used in the section on 'Isha to show covering and disappearance?
questions.answer: Darkness covering the day’s world, winter covering the earth, and old human traces being hidden by forgetfulness.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the world during 'Isha in relation to testing?
questions.answer: It says this world, which is a place of examination, will be shut down forever.

questions.question: Which prayer time most clearly calls attention to being awakened from heedlessness?
questions.answer: Maghrib does.

questions.question: Which prayer time most clearly points to Allah’s overwhelming power over the whole world?
questions.answer: 'Isha does.

questions.question: What is one main lesson taught through the description of 'Asr?
questions.answer: Later stages of life, history, and the year should remind a person of Allah’s mercy and actions.

questions.question: What is one main lesson taught through the description of Maghrib?
questions.answer: The setting of the day should remind a person of death, the end of worldly life, and the need to wake up spiritually.

questions.question: What is one main lesson taught through the description of 'Isha?
questions.answer: Nightfall shows how things are hidden, forgotten, and brought to an end under Allah’s mighty rule.

questions.question: How are 'Asr and Maghrib different in emphasis?
questions.answer: 'Asr stresses later stages and divine favors, while Maghrib stresses endings and awakening from heedlessness.

questions.question: How are Maghrib and 'Isha similar?
questions.answer: Both remind people that worldly things do not last and that Allah’s greatness appears in endings.

questions.question: How are Maghrib and 'Isha different?
questions.answer: Maghrib focuses more on warning and waking the heart, while 'Isha focuses more on covering, disappearance, and the final closing of the world.

questions.question: What can a student infer from the mention of forgotten human works at 'Isha?
questions.answer: A student can infer that fame, achievements, and worldly traces are temporary.

questions.question: Based on this passage, why are these prayer times important moments for reflection?
questions.answer: Because each one helps a believer remember big truths about life, death, the world, and Allah’s power, mercy, and greatness.
